intent: The row (or column) of a NavigationMenu's top-level entries, one NavigationMenuItem each.
typical_uses: The single list of entries directly inside a NavigationMenu

dont_use_when.situation: A list of links with no expanding entries and no shared panel

instead.target: a plain `nav` element holding a list of links
instead.note: NavigationMenuList only works inside a NavigationMenu root, whose shared popup and hover machinery a flat list of links does not need.

invariants.text: Arrow keys along the root's `orientation` (left and right for `horizontal`, up and down for `vertical`) move focus between the triggers and links of the list, and stop at the first and last entry instead of wrapping.

anti_patterns.dont: Put a NavigationMenuTrigger or NavigationMenuLink directly in the list
anti_patterns.do_instead: Wrap each entry in its own NavigationMenuItem; the item carries the value that ties a trigger to its content

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the list's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the list's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through navigation-menu.module.css, not through this.

bad.title: A link placed in the list with no item around it
bad.why: The list is a `ul`; an entry outside a NavigationMenuItem is an `a` directly inside it, which is not valid list markup.
